title: The boy in the tower
hookLine: his noble family locks him up to stop him becoming a Dominican

cards: A young friar walks the road in the white habit of a new preaching order. Then horsemen. His own brothers, soldiers, ride him down, the old lives say, and carry him home to the family castle.
His family were nobles with a plan for him: a respectable post in the Church, near home, with standing and land. Not a begging friar who owned nothing and preached wherever people would listen.
So they shut him in, and waited for him to change his mind. His name was Thomas Aquinas. A new block begins with him, in a locked room.

teach.h: A YEAR OR MORE, TRADITION SAYS.
teach.b: Tradition says the confinement lasted a long time, by some tellings a year or more. His mother wanted her son back; his brothers wanted the habit gone. Thomas stayed put, and stayed a Dominican.

teach.h: HE STUDIED AND TAUGHT HIS SISTERS.
teach.b: The old accounts say he read the Scriptures, studied Peter Lombard's book of theology, the Sentences, and taught his sisters. Tradition says one sister was so moved that she later gave her own life to God as a nun.
Then the hard scene, told plainly. The brothers, the story goes, sent a woman into his room to pull him away from his vows.

teach.h: A BURNING STICK, A CROSS ON THE WALL.
teach.b: Thomas grabbed a burning stick from the fire, drove her out, and marked a cross on the wall with it.
Tradition adds that he prayed, fell asleep, and dreamed of angels binding a cord around his waist, and was not troubled that way again. In the end the family gave up.

teach.h: LET DOWN IN A BASKET, BACK TO HIS ORDER.
teach.b: One telling has him let down from a window in a basket, back to his brothers in the order. The Summa, the long, careful book ahead, was written by a man who first had to decide what he was for.
His family's plan wasn't wicked. It was sensible, even generous. His call was quieter and poorer.

teach.h: NO MAN PUTTING HIS HAND TO THE PLOUGH.
teach.b: In Luke, in the Douay-Rheims, Jesus says: "No man putting his hand to the plough, and looking back, is fit for the kingdom of God." Catholics honor Thomas as a saint and a Doctor of the Church.
Before the arguments, there was a door he wouldn't let anyone close.

how: Catholics keep the feast of Saint Thomas Aquinas each year, and Dominicans and Catholic schools often tell the story of his confinement when they speak about holding to a vocation.

games.q: what does “the boy in the tower” mean?
o: a prince locked away to keep him from a throne
young Thomas Aquinas, held at home by his family
a monk who chose to live walled up in prayer

games.q: you're Thomas, shut in at your family's castle. your mother and brothers want you out of the friar's habit. what do you do?
o: give in and take the post they've planned.
stay, keep the habit, and use the time to study and teach.
slip away on the first night and never come home.
games.why: the old lives say he stayed put, studied, taught his sisters, and kept his vows, until the family gave up. no raging, no giving in.

practice: Bring to mind one yes that matters to you: a vow, a vocation, a promise to a person, a piece of work you know is yours.
Name what pulls against it today, tiredness, other people's plans, your own second thoughts, without fighting them, then rest your attention back on the yes.
If you pray, ask God for the grace to keep it; if you don't, simply hold it, like a hand on a plough.

wordCard.voice: The boy in the tower. Thomas Aquinas, shut in at home by his own family, who came out still a Dominican.

orig.note: Latin: a calling, a summons — the word behind vocation.

carryVoice: Your line: he kept his call. The arguments begin tomorrow, in his own book. Until tomorrow.
